Your digital product checkout is more than a payment button. 👀 If you sell ebooks, templates, courses, guides, Canva templates, or other digital products, you need to think about what happens after someone clicks “buy.” Before selling your first digital product, make sure you have: 1️⃣ Purchase terms — what the customer is actually agreeing to when they buy. 2️⃣ License & use restrictions — what they can and cannot do with your product. 3️⃣ Privacy Policy — especially if you’re collecting customer information. 4️⃣ Website/store terms — the rules governing purchases and use of your store. 5️⃣ Protection against unauthorized sharing & reselling — because your digital product should not become the internet’s free download. 😭 Your creativity is an asset. Treat it like one. And remember: your legal protection shouldn’t start after someone steals or misuses your digital product. It should be part of your business from the beginning. videos.caption: The process is. 👇 If you want to start selling digital products, here’s the simple step by step: 1️⃣ Pick ONE problem to solve Don’t create a random ebook and hope people buy it. Find a problem your audience already has. Examples: 🎨 “How do I use Canva?” 🐶 “How do I train my dog?” 🧘 “How do I build a better meditation routine?” The more specific the problem, the easier it is to create content around it. 2️⃣ Create a simple digital product 📕 You don’t need 100 pages. Create something that helps someone get from A → B. Think: ✅ Checklists ✅ Guides ✅ Templates ✅ Planners ✅ Workbooks ✅ Step by step instructions Your product should save someone time, confusion or frustration. 3️⃣ Create content that solves PART of the problem 🎥 This is where most beginners go wrong. They constantly say: “Buy my product!” Instead, teach. Give people something they can actually use. For example: ❌ “Buy my Canva guide.” ✅ “Here are 3 Canva mistakes making your designs look amateur.” Now you’re providing value AND attracting people who already have the problem your product solves. 4️⃣ Give them a reason to keep watching 👀 Use a simple structure: 🔥 Hook 📚 Value 🎯 Example 👉 Next step Example: “Your Canva designs look boring for one simple reason…” Then teach the reason. Show an example. Then tell them where they can learn the full process. 5️⃣ Post consistently 📈 You don’t need to be perfect. You need enough reps to learn what your audience responds to. Start with 1 piece of content per day. Then study: 👀 What gets watched? 💬 What gets comments? 🔄 What gets shared? 🔗 What gets clicks? 💰 What actually generates sales? Double down on what works. 6️⃣ Build trust before expecting sales 🤝 People don’t buy because you posted a link. They buy because they trust that you understand their problem and can help them solve it. Show: 📱 Your process 📚 What you're learning 🎥 Tutorials 💡 Tips 📊 Results 🧠 Mistakes you've made You’re not just selling a PDF. You’re selling a shortcut to a result. And remember… People can have opinions about what you’re doing. Let them. Your job isn’t to convince every person on the internet. Your job is to keep learning, keep creating and keep improving. 🚀 If you want to learn how I approach content + digital products, comment LEARN below and I’ll point you in the right direction. 👇
